title: Far Let Me Flee from Worldly Sin
description: Far Let Me Flee from Worldly Sin in Tonic Solfa to OLD HUNDREDTH, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: John Brownlie translated these words from the Greek service books for Hymns from the Morningland (Paisley, 1911).
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Long Metre (8.8.8.8), and this page sets them to OLD HUNDREDTH; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Far let me flee from world-ly sin, Nor look be-hind, but on-ward press; Lest the de-ceit that lurks with-in, Should link the soul to world-li-ness.

lines: Far let me flee from worldly sin,
Nor look behind, but onward press;
Lest the deceit that lurks within,
Should link the soul to worldliness.
Ah! whither shall I flee, my God?
There is no refuge but in Thee,
But in Thy grace my troubled soul
And in Thy Spirit's firm control,
A power to lift me nearer heaven.
Thus shall I flee from worldly sin,
Nor look behind, but onward press,
And daily fight, and daily win

source: John Brownlie, Hymns from the Morningland (1911)
licence: Public domain: John Brownlie died in 1925.
credits: Translated by John Brownlie (1857–1925) from the Greek, public domain, as printed in Hymns from the Morningland; set to OLD HUNDREDTH by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
